problem: The bullet says 'Do not use the angle between a line voltage and a line current.' In a balanced circuit this angle is exactly φ, the same load angle. In star, line current equals phase current and line voltage is the corresponding phase voltage shifted by 30°, so the angle between them is unchanged. In delta, line voltage equals phase voltage and line current is the phase current shifted by 30°, again unchanged. The warning is therefore false for every balanced case this chapter covers and can make a student distrust correct working.
fix: Replace with: 'In the √3 formula, φ is the phase angle of the load, the angle between phase voltage and phase current. In a balanced circuit the angle between line voltage and line current is the same φ, so either measurement gives the same power factor. Only with an unbalanced load does each phase have its own angle.'

problem: The chapter derives the √3 magnitude but never states the phase shift between line and phase voltage. Students are commonly asked for this, and it is also the reason the line-current derivation in delta works.
fix: Add one sentence after the magnitude result: 'The line voltage also leads the corresponding phase voltage (neutral to line) by 30°; in delta, the line current lags the corresponding phase current by 30°.'
